## Valid ejection targets
`p-2`, `p-4`, `p-5`, `p-6`, `p-8` — or "SKIP".
These are the ONLY names a ballot may carry. Every other player is already out of the game — ejected or dead — and naming one wastes your vote: an invalid target is struck to SKIP. Pick your target from this list, or SKIP.

## Who reported the body
`p-2` reported the body that opened this meeting. In this game self-report is weakly exculpatory: the impostor almost never reports its own kill, so being first to the scene is not by itself evidence of guilt. Do not vote `p-2` merely for having reported it — weigh them on the same testimony, contradiction flags, and memory as everyone else.

## How to decide
Your maximum suspicion among the living ejection targets is **0.59**;
the skip threshold is **0.60** (the §4.6 reference point).
That arithmetic is evidence, not a command — but it is the whole crew's shared reference: when the max sits below the threshold, SKIP is the sound call, and a case for ejecting anyway must rest on evidence you can cite below, never on momentum. Your suspicion levels above are your own accumulated evidence from the whole game — trust them over meeting rhetoric. A suspect two independent witnesses place at the scene, or whose account a verified flag broke, is a stronger case than one carried by a single voice. Remember the vent mechanic: an impostor vents BETWEEN rooms invisibly, so your own sightings of someone leaving or being elsewhere earlier do NOT clear them of a witnessed vent. If your strongest suspicion points at a row tagged OUT OF THE GAME, that case is already closed — the dead cannot be voted, so weigh only the LIVING targets and SKIP if none of them carries the case on its own. Every EJECT names its evidence: the transcript turn that convinced you (in "primary_reason_id"), or the [obs ...] memory line that did (in "primary_reason_observation_id") — a call you cannot source either way is a call to SKIP, and a SKIP needs no citation. Set "confidence" to your honest probability that the call is right, judged against the evidence you cite: do not report a confidence at or above the skip threshold for a target whose suspicion is below it.
